evidence.observation: §0 makes duplicate handling binding ("Count duplicate evidence separately from distinct rows.") and §2/§4 promise appends to "a locally owned fact", but the CG1 observable exit criterion is only "Append located rows to a locally owned fact under additive preview and apply. Keep prior rows and spans intact and validate the extended population." and §9 defines acceptance as "the issue reproduction and the criterion in §4 as an acceptance pair". No criterion or §9 verification entry exercises a duplicate observation (same row from two documents), a conflicting constraint between the new row and the existing population, or an ownership refusal (append to a fact the local model does not own), so the milestone can close without demonstrating the very behaviors §0 binds.

concerns.recommendation: Add explicit CG1 acceptance cases to §4/§9: identical row arriving from two distinct documents (counted as duplicate evidence, not two rows), a new row violating an existing constraint (refusal with stated order), and an append attempted against a non-locally-owned fact (refusal).
concerns.title: CG1 exit criterion omits the duplicate-evidence, conflict and ownership behavior §0 makes binding

evidence.observation: §2 says "Preview row moves and role rewrites together" but nowhere states that apply is atomic or what happens when the row move validates and the role rewrite refuses. The repository's existing evolution machinery declares transaction_scope "single-leaf CAS; no multi-file atomicity" (src/gnd/evolve/models.py:1291), so a combined row/role consolidation plausibly spans leaves; the plan names no mechanism and §9's CG3 verification ("accept one group, decline another, restart from the decision log...") contains no partial-failure or rollback case. §10 mentions "the atomic publication and summary contract" only for the external-population option, leaving the in-model path's atomicity unaddressed.

concerns.recommendation: State the apply atomicity contract for CG3 (single atomic publication or explicit compensation/rollback on mid-apply refusal) and add a §9 case that forces a role-rewrite refusal after a row move and asserts the model is byte-identical to its pre-apply state.
concerns.title: Atomicity of combined row-move/role-rewrite apply is unspecified and untested

evidence.observation: CG3's only termination semantics are "recompute candidates after apply and stop at the configured threshold" — the threshold's quantity (score, group count, rounds), its configuration site, and the group review ordering are never defined. Because each apply recomputes candidates, a merge can generate new candidates indefinitely; no maximum-rounds, no-progress, or work budget is stated. §6 offers only "Record work counters and the first refusal where limits apply", which measures work without bounding it, and §9's CG3 cases cover accept/decline/restart but never that the loop actually terminates when declines dominate or when applies keep producing candidates.

concerns.recommendation: Define the threshold (what it counts, where configured, review order), state a hard bound (max rounds or max reviewed groups per run), and add a §9 case asserting termination with the recorded counters when candidate regeneration would otherwise continue.
concerns.title: CG3 loop termination and bounded work are claimed but not defined or testable

evidence.observation: CG2's criterion lists five signal classes ("singleton types, role-player and reading shapes, name similarity, units and counted nouns") and §9 verifies only order stability ("shuffle model declaration order and compare candidate group IDs and cited spans") and evidence-carrying for one confusable pair. Nothing demonstrates recall: no fixture plants a known candidate per signal class (e.g., a unit mismatch or a counted-noun conflict) and asserts it is emitted, so "Index ... units and counted nouns" is not a demonstrable claim and a signal that silently produces nothing would pass every stated check.

concerns.recommendation: Add a per-signal seeded-candidate acceptance case: for each listed signal class, a fixture containing a known instance that must appear in the emitted candidates with its evidence location and score.
concerns.title: CG2 candidate completeness has no per-signal recall criterion

evidence.observation: §2/§4 write the CG1 behavior as decided — "Append located rows to a locally owned fact" — while §10 records "Choose append-only in-model storage or the external population requested in #338" as open and warns the external option "requires revising CG1". The plan thus presents milestone completion criteria that are explicitly provisional, and since #338 is described as requesting the external population, the proposed in-model behavior deviates from the issue without a recorded rationale; a reader approving §4 approves a criterion the plan itself says may be voided by D1.

concerns.recommendation: Either record the rationale for proposing in-model append against #338's requested external population, or mark the CG1 row of §4 conditional on D1 and add the external-population variant's exit criterion so both resolution outcomes have completion criteria.
concerns.title: CG1 exit criterion prejudges the open D1 storage decision and deviates from #338's requested option without rationale

evidence.observation: §2 names four review decisions — "record merge, demotion, subtype or leave" — but never defines what demotion or subtype do to the model, and §9 tests only the accept/decline pair, leaving two of the four decision kinds without any observable outcome. The decision log that "restart from the decision log" and declined-group suppression depend on has no artifact home in §3 (which names only src/gnd/evolve/policy.py and components), and the suppression key is unspecified: §2 requires "stable candidate IDs" and "recompute candidates after apply", but whether a declined group is recognized by candidate ID or by evidence identity after recomputation is unstated, so the §9 guarantee "not offered again unless its evidence changes" has no defined mechanism.

concerns.recommendation: Define each decision kind's model effect, name the decision log's home and identity key (candidate ID vs evidence hash) in §3, and extend §9 with a demotion and a subtype case plus a recompute-after-apply case showing a declined group stays suppressed under regenerated IDs.
concerns.title: Review-decision vocabulary, decision-log home and suppression keying are undefined

evidence.observation: §3 states "CG1 provides the canonical evidence representation for CG2 and CG3. Candidate discovery may read a model before CG1 ships, but the closure replay must exercise two documents and an accepted merge." Because D1 (§10) can still replace in-model evidence with an external population, CG2 indexing built before CG1 ships may target an evidence representation that is then revised, and the only checkpoint is the closure replay — which is also scoped to just "two documents and an accepted merge", exercising neither a declined group nor a role rewrite.

concerns.recommendation: Either gate CG2 implementation on D1's resolution, or state explicitly which evidence-representation assumptions CG2 may rely on pre-CG1; widen the closure replay to include a declined group and a role rewrite so the replay covers the decision-log and atomicity paths.
concerns.title: CG2 may start against an evidence representation that D1 can still invalidate, and the closure replay is narrowly scoped

evidence.observation: §6 repeats §0's first two sentences verbatim: "Document and check every new sample span against the cited document before CAS. Count duplicate evidence separately from distinct rows." Duplicated normative text in two sections invites divergence when one copy is later revised (e.g., after D1 resolves), leaving the binding rule and the risk control stating different things.

concerns.recommendation: Keep the normative statement once in §0 and have §6 reference it, adding only the genuinely risk-specific controls (fixture variation, work counters) in §6.
concerns.title: §6 restates §0's binding rules verbatim, risking divergent copies

summary: Plan r1 for cross-document growth is coherent and honest about its open decision, but its acceptance machinery does not demonstrate several behaviors the rubric and the plan's own binding rules name: duplicate-observation/provenance-conflict handling for #338 has no falsifiable case, CG3 row/role rewrite atomicity and loop termination are unspecified against a codebase whose CAS is explicitly single-leaf, CG2 candidate completeness has no recall test, and the CG1 exit criterion prejudges the still-open D1 storage decision.
